about: Awkward SQL for the two readers of schema.sql: scripts/check_destructive_ddl.py (tests/test_destructive_ddl_corpus.py) and web/tests/unit/schema-sql-scan.ts (web/tests/unit/schema.idempotency.test.ts). Both must report the same number of statements and the same unacknowledged findings for every case. Expectations are written by hand from PostgreSQL's lexical rules.

cases.name: two plain statements
cases.sql: SELECT 1; SELECT 2;

cases.name: no final semicolon
cases.sql: SELECT 1; SELECT 2

cases.name: empty statements
cases.sql: ;;; SELECT 1;; ;

cases.name: only whitespace and comments
cases.sql:
-- nothing
/* here */

cases.name: a semicolon in a string
cases.sql: SELECT 'a;b'; SELECT 2;

cases.name: a doubled quote in a string
cases.sql: SELECT 'it''s; fine'; SELECT 2;

cases.name: an E string with an escaped quote
cases.sql: SELECT E'it\'s; here'; SELECT 2;

cases.name: a plain string that ends in a backslash
cases.sql: SELECT 'a\'; SELECT 2;

cases.name: an E string holding a backslash pair
cases.sql: SELECT E'\\'; SELECT 2;

cases.name: B and X strings
cases.sql: SELECT B'101;', X'1F;'; SELECT 2;

cases.name: a letter that is not a string prefix
cases.sql: SELECT a'b;c'; SELECT 2;

cases.name: a dollar body with semicolons
cases.sql: DO $$ BEGIN NULL; NULL; END $$; SELECT 1;

cases.name: a tagged body
cases.sql: DO $body$ BEGIN NULL; END $body$; SELECT 1;

cases.name: a tag with an underscore and digits
cases.sql: DO $_t1$ BEGIN NULL; END $_t1$; SELECT 1;

cases.name: a tag with a non-ASCII letter
cases.sql: DO $é$ BEGIN NULL; END $é$; SELECT 1;

cases.name: $$ inside a tagged body
cases.sql: DO $a$ BEGIN PERFORM $$x;$$; END $a$; SELECT 1;

cases.name: two different tags nested
cases.sql: DO $a$ BEGIN EXECUTE $b$ SELECT 1; $b$; END $a$; SELECT 2;

cases.name: tags that differ only in case
cases.sql: SELECT $A$ x; $a$ y; $A$; SELECT 2;

cases.name: a parameter is not a quote
cases.sql: SELECT $1; SELECT $2;

cases.name: a dollar sign inside a word
cases.sql: SELECT a$b$c; SELECT 1;

cases.name: a tag cannot start with a digit
cases.sql: SELECT $1a$ x; SELECT 2;

cases.name: a line comment with a quote and a semicolon
cases.sql:
SELECT 1; -- it's; here
SELECT 2;

cases.name: a block comment with semicolons
cases.sql: /* a; b; */ SELECT 1;

cases.name: a nested block comment
cases.sql: /* a /* b; */ c; */ SELECT 1;

cases.name: a double dash inside a string
cases.sql: SELECT '--;'; SELECT 2;

cases.name: a block comment opener inside a string
cases.sql: SELECT '/*'; SELECT 2; SELECT '*/';

cases.name: a quoted identifier with a semicolon
cases.sql: SELECT "a;b" FROM t; SELECT 2;

cases.name: a doubled quote in a quoted identifier
cases.sql: SELECT "a"";b"; SELECT 2;

cases.name: non-ASCII text
cases.sql:
SELECT 'é;ü'; -- café;
SELECT 2;

cases.name: CRLF line ends
cases.sql:
SELECT 1;
SELECT 2;

cases.name: a string never closed
cases.sql: SELECT 'a; SELECT 2;

cases.name: an E string whose last quote is escaped
cases.sql: SELECT E'a\'; SELECT 2;

cases.name: a dollar quote never closed
cases.sql: DO $$ BEGIN NULL; END;

cases.name: a tagged quote closed by another tag
cases.sql: DO $a$ BEGIN NULL; END $b$;

cases.name: a block comment never closed
cases.sql: SELECT 1; /* a /* b */

cases.name: a quoted identifier never closed
cases.sql: SELECT "a; SELECT 2;

cases.sql: UPDATE builds SET status = 'LIVE';

cases.name: mixed case with spaces
cases.sql: UPDATE builds SET status = ' Live ';

cases.name: an INSERT
cases.sql: INSERT INTO builds (status) VALUES ('live');

cases.name: a MERGE
cases.sql: MERGE INTO builds b USING s ON b.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET status = 'live';

cases.name: in a WITH query
cases.sql: WITH x AS (UPDATE builds SET status = 'live' RETURNING id) SELECT * FROM x;

cases.name: in a string handed to EXECUTE
cases.sql: DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'UPDATE builds SET status = ''live'''; END $$;

cases.name: EXECUTE format with the value as an argument
cases.sql: DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE format('UPDATE %I SET status = %L', 'builds', 'live'); END $$;

cases.name: in a dollar-quoted string handed to EXECUTE
cases.sql: DO $a$ BEGIN EXECUTE $b$UPDATE builds SET status = 'live'$b$; END $a$;

cases.name: in a DO inside a string handed to EXECUTE
cases.sql: DO $a$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'DO $b$ BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = ''live''; END $b$'; END $a$;

cases.name: in a function body
cases.sql: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void AS $$ BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = 'live'; END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

cases.name: the tag $m$
cases.sql: DO $m$ BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = 'live'; END $m$;

cases.name: the tag $_$
cases.sql: DO $_$ BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = 'live'; END $_$;

cases.name: the tag $a1$
cases.sql: DO $a1$ BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = 'live'; END $a1$;

cases.name: the tag $body$
cases.sql: DO $body$ BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = 'live'; END $body$;

cases.name: the tag $é$
cases.sql: DO $é$ BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = 'live'; END $é$;

cases.name: a block comment between DO and the tag
cases.sql: DO /* x */ $m$ BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = 'live'; END $m$;

cases.name: a line comment between DO and the tag
cases.sql:
DO -- x
$m$ BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = 'live'; END $m$;

cases.name: a value carried through a variable is not followed
cases.sql: DO $$ DECLARE s text := 'live'; BEGIN UPDATE builds SET status = s; END $$;

cases.name: a value built by concatenation is not followed
cases.sql: UPDATE builds SET status = 'li' || 've';

cases.name: a string written with escapes is not decoded
cases.sql: UPDATE builds SET status = E'\x6c\x69ve';

cases.name: live_url is not live
cases.sql: UPDATE builds SET live_url = 'https://x.example/page' WHERE id = 1;

cases.name: a string that holds live_url
cases.sql: UPDATE builds SET note = 'see live_url' WHERE id = 1;

cases.name: a WHERE that reads live is refused too
cases.sql: UPDATE builds SET is_harbor = true WHERE status = 'live';

cases.name: DELETE cannot write a status
cases.sql: DELETE FROM builds WHERE status = 'live';

cases.name: SELECT may read it
cases.sql: SELECT * FROM builds WHERE status = 'live';

cases.name: a CHECK constraint may list it
cases.sql: ALTER TABLE builds ADD CONSTRAINT c CHECK (status IN ('queued', 'live'));

cases.name: a default of live
cases.sql: ALTER TABLE builds ALTER COLUMN status SET DEFAULT 'live';

cases.name: a default of live in parentheses
cases.sql: ALTER TABLE builds ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS s TEXT DEFAULT ('live');

cases.name: a default of live in CREATE TABLE
cases.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS t (status TEXT DEFAULT 'live');

cases.name: another default
cases.sql: ALTER TABLE builds ALTER COLUMN status SET DEFAULT 'queued';

cases.name: a comment that names the statement
cases.sql: COMMENT ON TABLE builds IS 'UPDATE builds SET status = live is done in application code';
